title: Money page, round 3 — the bigger choices

steps.path: Behind the charts, bills and payment links
steps.headline: Should the page start reading your purchases, and where should they be kept?
steps.today: The page only reads balances. You chose "balances only" in round 1, so nothing about individual purchases is fetched or saved.
steps.problem: Spending over time, finding your subscriptions, and linking every Netflix payment across accounts all need the list of purchases. Without it those features cannot exist.
steps.proposal: The app fetches your purchases through Plaid (already included in the free tier) and keeps them. Pick where.

options.label: On this computer only
options.summary: Purchases stay in the app's own storage on this laptop, like your bank sign-ins. The page asks the app for totals and lists when it needs them.
pros: Purchases never sync to GitHub or anywhere else.
No size limit, so years of history fit.
cons: Your other computer shows balances but not spending charts or payment history.

options.label: With the page (syncs)
options.summary: Purchases are saved in the page's data, next to your balances.
cons: Every purchase lands in your sync repo's history forever.
Pages are capped at 1 MB, so only a few months fit.

options.label: Keep balances only
cons: No spending charts, no subscription finding, no payment linking.

steps.path: The big chart at the top, with buttons to switch what it shows
steps.headline: Which charts should the top chart switch between?
steps.today: There is one chart: net worth over time.
steps.problem: Net worth alone hides what is actually moving: one account, your spending, or your debt going down.
steps.proposal: A row of buttons above the chart switches what it draws. Pick every chart you want; each keeps the same time buttons (1W, 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, All).

options.label: Net worth
options.summary: What you have minus what you owe.

options.label: One account
options.summary: Pick any account and see its balance over time.
pros: See a card climb or a loan shrink.

options.label: Monthly spending
options.summary: Each month's spending as bars, split by category (food, shopping, bills...).
pros: Where the money goes, month to month.

options.label: Bills & subscriptions
options.summary: What your repeating bills and subscriptions cost each month, and how that total changes.

options.label: Debt paydown
options.summary: Total owed over time, with each card and loan as a band.

options.label: Money in vs out
options.summary: Each month: what came in (paychecks) and what went out.
pros: Whether you are ahead each month.

steps.path: Add an account by hand, and every account card
steps.headline: Should each kind of account get its own fields and its own card layout?
steps.today: Every hand-added account uses the same form: balance, limit, interest, payment. An Affirm plan looks like a checking account.
steps.problem: An Affirm plan cares about payments left and the last payment date; a checking account cares about none of that. One form fits nothing well.
steps.proposal: Each kind asks only for what matters and its card shows only that: Checking/Savings (balance), Credit card (limit, interest, due date, minimum), Loan (rate, payment, payoff), Pay-later plan like Affirm or layaway (total, payments left, how often, last payment), Investment (value), and Something you own like a car (value, updated by hand). Yes builds it; No keeps one form.

steps.headline: Use this list of categories for bills and spending?
steps.today: Bills have no category; they are only a name and a company.
steps.problem: Without categories the page cannot total "what do my subscriptions cost" or split spending into meaningful slices.
steps.proposal: Every bill and payment gets one category, picked from: Housing, Utilities, Phone & internet, Insurance, Subscriptions, Transportation (car payment, gas), Loans, Credit cards, Pay-later plans, Health, Other. Yes uses this list; Don't know if you'd change it — say how in the note.

steps.path: Opening a bill such as Netflix
steps.headline: How should a bill find its past payments across your accounts?
steps.today: A bill you add (Netflix) knows nothing about the payments your banks have seen.
steps.problem: You want to open Netflix and see every payment you've made for it, whichever card or account paid it.
steps.proposal: Once purchases are read, an opened bill lists every matching payment, with totals for the last month, year, and all time. Pick how matches are found.

options.label: Suggest, you confirm
options.summary: The page finds payments whose name looks like the bill ("NETFLIX.COM") and shows them as suggestions; you tick the right ones once, and later ones that look the same link automatically.
cons: A minute of ticking the first time per bill.

options.label: Fully automatic
cons: Can mislink look-alikes (Apple Music vs App Store).

steps.headline: Trim a closed account card to bank, name, balance and one useful line?
steps.today: A closed card shows the bank under the name, a "Connected" label, a link button, an arrow, and for cards a bar with "% used · $ left".
steps.problem: "Connected" repeats on every card and the link button and arrow crowd the row, so the useful part is harder to see.
steps.proposal: Closed card: bank name small on top, account name, balance, and one line that changes by kind — card: % used and next due; loan: next payment and payoff month; checking: change this month. "Connected" only appears when something is wrong, and the link moves inside the opened card. Yes trims it; No keeps today's card.
